MC	<p>7455_4e4e</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #914521;">Gene P</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #914521;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #914521;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006b6e;">Gene W</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006b6e;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006b6e;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, pw, ++, pw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006b6e;">Gene W</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006b6e;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>55ab_a434</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #76590a;">Gene E</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #76590a;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #76590a;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006b6e;">Gene Y</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006b6e;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006b6e;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, ey, ++, ey"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>ab0e_86a4</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #646102;">Gene A</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #646102;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #646102;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #245bb1;">Gene T</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #245bb1;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #245bb1;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, at, ++, at"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>03a1_ffc9</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006e5a;">Gene R</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006e5a;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e5a;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #763cac;">Gene T</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #763cac;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9f3238;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e5a;">Gene D</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006e5a;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>63f0_eaa3</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #496923;">Gene P</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #496923;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #496923;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9d2c63;">Gene W</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #9d2c63;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9d2c63;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, pw, ++, pw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>7238_dc8a</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #00697f;">Gene C</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #00697f;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697f;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9d2c63;">Gene N</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #9d2c63;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>e2af_0b84</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #496923;">Gene A</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #496923;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #496923;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1d648f;">Gene P</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #1d648f;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>fdc9_930c</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #646102;">Gene A</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #646102;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #646102;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9d2c63;">Gene T</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #9d2c63;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9d2c63;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, at, ++, at"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #496923;">Gene C</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #496923;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #496923;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #245bb1;">Gene E</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #245bb1;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #914521;">Gene J</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #914521;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>8bd6_05fa</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #76590a;">Gene F</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #76590a;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #76590a;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #245bb1;">Gene W</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #245bb1;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #245bb1;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, fw, ++, fw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9f3238;">Gene H</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #9f3238;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9f3238;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697f;">Gene R</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #00697f;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #76590a;">Gene B</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #76590a;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>caa6_e809</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #76590a;">Gene H</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #76590a;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #76590a;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006b6e;">Gene T</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006b6e;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006b6e;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, ht, ++, ht"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #874e00;">Gene D</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #874e00;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #874e00;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1d648f;">Gene T</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #1d648f;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>3240_a580</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #00697f;">Gene F</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #00697f;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697f;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9d2c63;">Gene X</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #9d2c63;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9d2c63;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, fx, ++, fx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 5px 8px;">2,000</td></tr></table><h6>Step-by-Step Instructions</h6><ul> <li>Step 1: Find the row for the Parental Type for all three genes.</li> <li>Step 2: Looking at only your two genes, assign PD, NPD, TT.</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul> <li>Step 4: Determine the map distance between the two genes.</li> <ul><li>D = &half; (TT + 6 NPD) / total = (3 NPD + &half; TT) / total</li></ul></ul><h5>Determine the distance between the two genes MC	<p>a2b2_734b</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #914521;">Gene F</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #914521;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>b4b2_784b</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006b6e;">Gene N</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006b6e;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006b6e;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8e318d;">Gene P</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #8e318d;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006e5a;">Gene F</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006e5a;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e5a;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8e318d;">Gene J</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #8e318d;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8e318d;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, fj, ++, fj"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. Looking at only your two genes, assign PD, NPD, TT.</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul> <li>Step 4: Determine the map distance between the two genes.</li> <ul><li>D = &half; (TT + 6 NPD) / total = (3 NPD + &half; TT) / total</li></ul></ul><h5>Determine the distance between the two genes MC	<p>0a78_98f7</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #496923;">Gene E</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #496923;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #496923;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1d648f;">Gene F</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #1d648f;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1d648f;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, ef, ++, ef"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #646102;">Gene H</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #646102;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #76590a;">Gene J</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #76590a;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>5a23_e5e1</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #874e00;">Gene E</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #874e00;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #874e00;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #763cac;">Gene M</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #763cac;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #763cac;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, em, ++, em"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>bf19_b52e</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #646102;">Gene H</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #646102;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #646102;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8e318d;">Gene K</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #8e318d;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #76590a;">Gene A</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #76590a;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #76590a;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006b6e;">Gene H</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006b6e;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006b6e;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, ah, ++, ah"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>0490_a0b1</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #914521;">Gene C</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #914521;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #914521;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #544db6;">Gene H</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #544db6;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #544db6;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, ch, ++, ch"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>0d40_a3d3</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006e5a;">Gene N</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006e5a;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e5a;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #763cac;">Gene W</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #763cac;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>66c4_11a5</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #496923;">Gene R</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #496923;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #496923;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1d648f;">Gene W</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #1d648f;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1d648f;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, rw, ++, rw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>8d16_02aa</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #00697f;">Gene K</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #00697f;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697f;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8e318d;">Gene M</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #8e318d;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8e318d;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, km, ++, km"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9f3238;">Gene D</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #9f3238;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9f3238;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #245bb1;">Gene W</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #245bb1;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>9478_8ff7</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006e5a;">Gene B</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006e5a;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e5a;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9d2c63;">Gene H</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #9d2c63;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9d2c63;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, bh, ++, bh"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>d36f_af3d</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #76590a;">Gene H</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #76590a;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #76590a;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8e318d;">Gene Y</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #8e318d;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8e318d;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, hy, ++, hy"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>931f_870a</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #646102;">Gene A</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #646102;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #646102;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #245bb1;">Gene W</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #245bb1;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #245bb1;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, aw, ++, aw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>a2a1_2038</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #236e3f;">Gene C</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #236e3f;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #236e3f;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #245bb1;">Gene W</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #245bb1;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #245bb1;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, cw, ++, cw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #646102;">Gene A</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #646102;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #646102;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #245bb1;">Gene M</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #245bb1;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>9647_798d</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9f3238;">Gene B</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #9f3238;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9f3238;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #245bb1;">Gene F</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #245bb1;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>9eaf_0066</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9f3238;">Gene C</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #9f3238;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9f3238;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e5a;">Gene N</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006e5a;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e5a;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, cn, ++, cn"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9f3238;">Gene D</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #9f3238;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9f3238;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #496923;">Gene H</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #496923;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>98a2_fa03</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #496923;">Gene H</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #496923;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #496923;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #763cac;">Gene P</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #763cac;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #763cac;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, hp, ++, hp"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>95f2_2541</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #00697f;">Gene A</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #00697f;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697f;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8e318d;">Gene N</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #8e318d;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8e318d;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, an, ++, an"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #874e00;">Gene M</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #874e00;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #874e00;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006b6e;">Gene X</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006b6e;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>2ab5_5167</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #236e3f;">Gene T</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #236e3f;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #236e3f;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #544db6;">Gene X</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #544db6;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #544db6;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, tx, ++, tx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>be43_f40e</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #646102;">Gene M</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #646102;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #646102;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1d648f;">Gene P</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #1d648f;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #874e00;">Gene J</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #874e00;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>72a0_ad31</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #496923;">Gene D</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #496923;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #496923;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #763cac;">Gene N</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #763cac;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>5215_0674</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #646102;">Gene B</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #646102;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #646102;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #245bb1;">Gene Y</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #245bb1;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #245bb1;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, by, ++, by"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral.
